palette.role: Evergreen continuity in side zones through winter.

leafHabit.basis: RHS: evergreen. BSBI calls it winter-green or semi-deciduous and Flora of China semi-evergreen: expect leaf loss in exposed or cold sites.

handedness.basis: No written source gives the direction for this species (searched in English, German, Japanese and Chinese, November 2026). Read by this project from two photographs of identified plants on Wikimedia Commons: in both, the near side of each coil round the support runs from upper left to lower right, a left-handed helix (clockwise seen from above). They are "Lonicera acuminata kz03.jpg" (Botanischer Garten Berlin-Dahlem, 2017) and "Korina 2017-08-01 Lonicera henryi 2.jpg" (a stem on a metal post). That agrees with the genus: Darwin records L. brachypoda (L. japonica) as following the sun, and L. periclymenum twines clockwise seen from above. Photographs and congeners, not a published statement: check a specimen before relying on it.

attachment.supportNeeds: Reachable slender members or cables in partial shade, with access for trimming.

wood.basis: Inferred, not stated anywhere for this species. Gardens Illustrated names L. henryi among the later-flowering honeysuckles that are tidied in spring, as against L. periclymenum, which it says flowers on the previous year's stems; the RHS honeysuckle guide says late-flowering types "flower on the current season's growth". Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): the flowers come "at the end of the shoot". The RHS record gives pruning group 11 with no timing, which would have settled it.

monthsUK.basis: RHS record: flowers "in summer", which is June to August by the season rule (spring = Mar-May, summer = Jun-Aug, autumn = Sep-Nov, winter = Dec-Feb; early, mid and late are the first, second and third month). Only June is stated outright: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online) says the flowers are "produced during June". July and August rest on the RHS season word alone.

flowering.display: Small yellow and red tubular flowers, then black berries.

site.aspect: Full sun or partial shade; north, east or west facing; exposed or sheltered, though leaf persistence is site-specific.

calendar.note: Spring: remove congested or dead shoots and shorten long shoots that leave their space (Gardens Illustrated, naming L. henryi; RHS honeysuckle guide for late-flowering types, which warns that a hard prune reduces flowering). RHS record: pruning group 11, no timing given. Check for nesting birds first.
RHS honeysuckle guide: mulch in spring to reduce water stress and the risk of powdery mildew; feed once in spring if wanted.

management.notes: Control competitive overgrowth, thin to preserve neighbours, inspect attachments, and watch berries in visitor spaces. Contain it: it spreads by bird-sown seed.

hazards: Fruit is ornamental and not to be eaten (RHS).

regional.status: Not legally listed. A naturalised neophyte, bird-sown and extending its range in woodland margins, hedgerows and rough grassland (BSBI).
EPPO Alert List since 2019 (as Lonicera acuminata); invasive in Swiss forests.
